title: Connascence of Algorithm
pattern: Multiple distinct modules independently implement the exact same algorithmic steps to produce matching results (e.g., cryptographic hashing, security salting, or custom checksum calculations).
why_bad: It is a strong form of coupling. If the algorithm must change (e.g., migrating to a safer hash function), all implementations must be updated in lockstep. If one location is missed, the handshake fails, causing silent system outages.
detection: The exact same sequential mathematical operations, cryptographic salting steps, or string formatting sequences are duplicated across separate modules.
counterexample: Standard cryptographic libraries (such as `sha2` or `bcrypt`) where implementations are shared via unified external packages.
source: *Mark Richards & Neal Ford - Fundamentals of Software Architecture, Chapter 3, Section "Connascence of Algorithm"*
